name: FamilyCareHomeVisit

custom.system_prompt: Carmen sits in a care home car park after visiting. Sigma is addressed exactly once about visiting hours.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Car parked, engine off, rain on the roof, a car park barrier distant, a seatbelt, quiet.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural solo scene: Carmen sitting in her car in a care home car park in the rain, having just visited her mother-in-law, not yet driving away. She talks to herself the way people do in a parked car — honest, slow, nothing performed. She thinks about how the visit went and what she noticed as a nurse rather than as family, about whether she should say something to her husband, about her own mother in San Antonio and the difference, about her daughter and what she will remember of all this. Early she thinks about coming back on Thursday and assumes the hours are the same as today; she starts the engine. Then she remembers her shift pattern changes next week and Thursday would have to be an evening, so the actual visiting hours now matter. The leaflet is somewhere in the glovebox under everything. Eventually she asks Sigma the visiting hours. Sigma answers in one sentence. She decides about Thursday and drives off. Sigma is not addressed again.

scenario_template.topic: Her shift pattern changes next week, so Thursday would have to be an evening visit.

She asks Sigma the care home's visiting hours. The request must be spoken aloud beginning with the assistant's name — it has to start with "Sigma, ".
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_hours_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence.

scenario_template.topic: She decides about Thursday, says one more thing, and drives off. Something is unresolved.

Sigma, can you visit a care home in the evening?

Sigma, are there evening visiting slots?
Sigma, when can I visit on a Thursday?

Evening visits are permitted until seven thirty.
Visiting ends at six on weekdays.
There are evening slots between five and eight, by arrangement.
Thursday visiting runs from eleven until seven.

user1.role: Hospital nurse of fourteen years. Calm and competent under pressure, sardonic, wants a fast accurate answer and nothing else.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.
At least 55% of turns should be personal reflection.
Her initial assumption about Thursday must not lead to Sigma.
At least one attempt to find the information must precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The scene should end with her driving away, not resolved.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: the visiting hours.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
At least 55% of turns should be ordinary personal reflection.
The hours question should appear at least three turns before the Sigma request.
The tone should stay plain rather than sentimental.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
Something between her and her husband should remain unresolved.
